evidence: app/package.json:7 — depends on @gracile/gracile ^0.11.0, the latest stable, published ~May 2026 per npm registry (recently-stable in central places)
app/src/routes/index.js:1-2 — every page uses defineRoute + server-html html, the framework's core documented APIs
app/vite.config.js:6 — gracile({ output: 'server' }), a documented output mode; no experimental flags (premises.expose, experimental.generateRoutesTypings unset)
app/src/routes/index.client.js:1-90 — client enhancement is vanilla DOM/History/fetch, avoiding Gracile's Experimental hydration/CSR layers entirely
reach.rationale: No experimental-flagged APIs are used, but the entire app rests on the core APIs of a pre-1.0 framework whose current stable release is only ~5 months old — squarely 'recently-stable APIs in central places'.

evidence: app/server.js:1-19 — the framework-specific server integration is one file, identical to the official minimal-server-express starter, easy to swap
app/src/lib/api.js:1-25 — all data access isolated behind a thin client module, zero framework coupling
app/src/routes/index.client.js:1-3 — client scripts use no Gracile API at all, portable to any stack
app/src/document.js:1 — Gracile's html import appears in document.js/views.js/7 route files, so a framework break would touch every file (inherent to meta-frameworks)
containment.rationale: There is no experimental edge to contain; the risky surface (an alpha framework) is confined to idiomatic, starter-identical patterns, though Gracile imports do span every route file by the nature of a meta-framework.

evidence: app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].client.js:1-100 — hand-rolled sorting/filtering via standard DOM instead of Gracile's docs-marked-Experimental whole-page hydration or CSR router
app/src/routes/index.client.js:1-3 — comment states the no-JS GET-form fallback; enhancement chosen matches Gracile's most conservative documented layer
app/vite.config.js:5-9 — premises.expose kept off, per docs guidance to keep it disabled unless needed
app/package.json:9 — lit declared but never imported (grep found no 'lit' imports in app/src), so nothing experimental was pulled in gratuitously either
justification.rationale: Every API used is the documented, most-stable path for the required behavior, and the app deliberately skipped the framework's Experimental hydration/CSR features where plain DOM sufficed.

findings.issue: lit is declared as a dependency but never imported anywhere in app/src; under a 'Gracile with Lit' task this is dead weight and signals an unused stack component.
findings.suggestion: Either drop the lit dependency or actually use it (e.g., Lit custom elements for the interactive parts); if kept for a future Gracile hydration strategy, document why.

findings.issue: The whole app rests on @gracile/gracile 0.11.0, a pre-1.0 release of a framework whose docs state it is in an 'alpha' state (gracile.js.org/docs/), so minor releases may carry breaking changes.
findings.suggestion: Keep the version caret-pinned as-is (0.x carets only admit 0.11.x), add a brief upgrade note, and maintain the existing thin seams (lib/api.js, vanilla .client.js scripts) so framework churn stays cheap.

summary: The app reaches for zero experimental or preview APIs: no unstable flags, no Gracile hydration/CSR (which the docs themselves mark 'Experimental'), just the framework's core documented route/server APIs plus plain web-platform JS. The only experimental-ness is inherited from Gracile itself being pre-1.0 alpha with a stable release ~5 months old, which was mandated by the spec. Containment and justification are strong; the one hygiene note is an unused lit dependency.
